title: Medical Equipment Resale — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Field worksheets for buying surplus hospital gear cheap, proving it safe on the bench, and keeping every resale, rental, and refurbishment inside FDA rules, built from the numbers and warnings of refurbishers, biomeds, auction houses, and regulatory practitioners

worksheets.title: The Resale Engine: Capital, Sourcing, Listings, Freight, and Export Targets
worksheets.purpose: Lock in the core resale engine practitioners describe: buy surplus hospital gear cheap, document and biomed-check it, then resell or rerent it. This worksheet forces decisions on launch capital, surplus channels, high-demand items, inspection standards, listing disclosures, rental cycles, first hires, refurbisher vetting, freight insurance, and the first cross-border buyer profile.
instructions: Fill every field with your own numbers, names, and dates, using the cited practitioner example only as a benchmark to measure your plan against.
Write capital, volume, and price figures as specific dollar amounts or unit counts, never as ranges you have not checked against a real quote or invoice.
Where a field asks for a rule, phrase it as a hard yes-or-no test a new employee could apply on the warehouse floor without asking you.
Treat the biomed check, listing disclosure, refurbisher vetting, and freight insurance fields as gates: no unit ships until each one has a written answer.
Revisit the sourcing and export fields every quarter, comparing your actual inventory turn and buyer response against the benchmarks you recorded here.

fields.name: capital_plan
fields.prompt: Write down the liquid capital you can commit today, then decide whether you are launching a lean resale operation or a licensed Medicare-billing rental company, and list which licenses, warehouse space, and first hire each path would demand from you.
fields.example: The Earn Your Leisure founder started with $700,000 liquid and needed 6-7 licenses per location to bill Medicare [Earn Your Leisure — hQY0qIkQ-xY @ 00:02:44]. A Florida starter pitch claims a $4,000 lean launch. My plan: start lean with $4,000 reselling surplus gear, and revisit the Medicare rental path once cash reserves can support licensing.

fields.name: surplus_sources
fields.prompt: List every surplus channel you will work for inventory, including hospital liquidations, surplus auctions, manufacturer trade-in programs, and reseller pickups, and note the expected monthly volume and turn rate you would need from each channel.
fields.example: Centurion Service Group moves about 6,000 pieces a month for well over 1,000 hospitals, surgery centers and manufacturers, and turns its entire inventory every 5 weeks [Centurion Service Group: A TRIMEDX Company — dUZz08G_Dzc @ 00:00:21]. My benchmark: bid on regional hospital surplus lots weekly and target a full inventory turn inside two months while I build volume.

fields.name: high_demand_skus
fields.prompt: Name the specific high-demand items you will hunt first, explain why buyers want them, and pair each with the accessories that make it easier to sell, such as lifts that fit underneath beds or matching components buyers request together.
fields.example: Stryker bassinets are called high demand, progressive beds hard to find, and GlideScope systems always in demand [Used Medical Equipment — 0jN0a_8CpgI @ 00:01:08]. Low-base Hoyer lifts like the Linux and Leos suit progressive hospital beds because they go low enough to fit underneath [Used Medical Equipment — 0jN0a_8CpgI @ 00:01:57]. I will bundle any progressive bed with a low-base lift.

fields.name: biomed_check
fields.prompt: Describe the exact inspection each unit receives before it ships, who performs the biomed check, and how you label anything that has not been fully verified, so no item leaves your floor on a power-on test alone.
fields.example: Bill Whittemore warns that sellers who see the lights come on, call it good and ship it are hurting the industry [Bill Whittemore — zLW0PtGvqQE @ 00:11:23]. His rule is to recheck with a biomed team or sell explicitly as is [Bill Whittemore — zLW0PtGvqQE @ 00:12:05]. My standard: every unit gets a biomed recheck or an as-is tag.

fields.name: listing_standards
fields.prompt: Draft the condition disclosure template you will attach to every online listing, including the known limits of the item, the photo angles required, and the wording that sets buyer expectations before a return request ever arrives.
fields.example: Jon Sheppard Sells calls medical items the biggest return in profits of anything picked up over years of reselling [Jon Sheppard Sells — 8meyld3BWGg @ 00:00:19], yet warns returns still hit sellers who claimed nothing, so condition limits and clear pictures go into the listing before it goes live [Jon Sheppard Sells — 8meyld3BWGg @ 00:03:44]. My template opens with known flaws.

fields.name: rental_model
fields.prompt: If you plan to rent rather than sell, map the rental cycle for your core equipment, the pickup trigger when a patient no longer needs it, and the steps required before the same unit is rerented to the next patient.
fields.example: The Earn Your Leisure founder describes a 13-month rental for most equipment; if a patient passes away, goes into the hospital or no longer needs it, the unit is picked up and rerented [Earn Your Leisure — hQY0qIkQ-xY @ 00:08:26]. Every Medicare-primary patient is run through the one-per-five-years wheelchair rule before delivery [Earn Your Leisure — hQY0qIkQ-xY @ 00:07:57].

fields.name: first_hire_and_stockpile
fields.prompt: Identify your first hire and the referral relationships that person brings, then estimate the orders those relationships could send your way and describe the stockpile you would build ahead of a supply disruption to fill them.
fields.example: The Earn Your Leisure founder made a salesperson the first hire, the son of a rehab director overseeing three rehab centers [Earn Your Leisure — hQY0qIkQ-xY @ 00:09:26]. When COVID hit, the founder filled a roughly 7,000 square foot ranch warehouse floor to roof and avoided most supply chain issues [Earn Your Leisure — hQY0qIkQ-xY @ 00:10:17].

fields.name: refurbisher_vetting
fields.prompt: List the questions you will put to every refurbishment provider before payment, covering HIPAA data removal, internal decontamination, pre-ship quality results, and proof that the system runs within the original manufacturer's specifications on an unedited recording.
fields.example: Block Imaging says to get the HIPAA data-removal step, internal decontamination and pre-ship QA results confirmed before payment [Block Imaging — xvO7-DA6X2w @ 00:01:37], and to demand an unedited functionality video proving the system runs within original manufacturer specifications [Block Imaging — xvO7-DA6X2w @ 00:03:05]. DES Technologies adds audit reports so data erasure is verifiable [DES Technologies — xzb3hv6fB4g @ 00:01:19].

fields.name: freight_plan
fields.prompt: Outline how you will move high-value equipment, including the carrier's medical freight history, whether trucks offer air-ride and climate control, and how you confirm the insurance coverage matches the freight value before the pickup is scheduled.
fields.example: Ntwdequiptrans says to confirm the carrier has moved medical loads before and that its insurance lines up with the freight value before the wheels start turning, especially on six-figure machines [Ntwdequiptrans — LXOka69hkxs @ 00:01:55]. My rule: no pickup on any imaging or lab system until the carrier's insurance coverage meets my invoice value.

fields.name: export_targets
fields.prompt: Choose your first cross-border market and define the buyer profile you will target there, including facility size, location, and the equipment tier those buyers will accept, plus how you will handle leads in their language.
fields.example: Global Health Intelligence filtered 195 targets from 1,800-plus Brazilian private institutions at 100-plus beds [Global Health Intelligence — FzWeG7sw7qk @ 00:01:46]. Healthcare Direct USA says tier three gear no longer moves into Latin America [Healthcare Direct USA — 09hrQ3SQK3E @ 00:10:03] and routes unanswered messages to email after about 15 minutes, sending Spanish-speaking buyers to Spanish-speaking reps [Healthcare Direct USA — 09hrQ3SQK3E @ 00:20:15].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 1 is complete only when every field names a specific dollar figure, channel, or rule; the biomed check field forbids shipping on a power-on test alone; the refurbisher field requires HIPAA data removal, decontamination, and pre-ship QA before payment; and the freight field ties carrier insurance to invoice value.

worksheets.title: The Service Bench: Rates, Memberships, Parts Vetting, Safety Testing, and Stop Rules
worksheets.purpose: Turn the third-party biomed playbook into a working service operation. Practitioners say the edge comes from people, parts, and paperwork, and that every bench reading starts with a proven analyzer. This worksheet sets rate cards, recurring memberships, contractor insurance, parts supplier vetting, service report fields, bidding floors, and the electrical safety sequence and stop rules every technician follows.
instructions: Price every service line from your real costs of labor, parts, travel, and shipping before comparing your numbers to the practitioner benchmarks cited.
Write each vetting and insurance check as a document you can file, so an auditor or customer can see proof rather than a verbal promise.
Record electrical safety limits as exact numbers with units, such as microamps, ohms, megohms, and amps, and never as general pass or fail notes.
Run the analyzer verification steps before filling in the test sequence field, and record the actual stud readings you got on your own meter.
Treat the stop rules as binding: any condition listed there halts the job until recalibration, service intervention, or a root-cause repair is documented.

fields.name: service_rate_card
fields.prompt: Build your service rate card line by line, separating labor, parts, travel, and shipping, and set your regular hourly rate, after-hours rate, and the travel threshold beyond which a customer pays an added trip charge.
fields.example: Jason of Bright Idea Dental Repair bills four lines, labor, parts, travel and shipping, at $175 an hour regular, $225 after hours, and $75 travel beyond 30 minutes [Better Biomed Channel — YXLWY7VHfxM @ 00:35:36]. He launched on $8,000 of test gear and first priced at $150 an hour before raising to $175.

fields.name: pm_membership
fields.prompt: Design a recurring preventive maintenance membership for your clinic customers, stating the monthly price, what each visit includes, the revenue target per technician, and the part-time role you would add so the shop can run without you.
fields.example: Jason sells $200-a-month PM memberships and targets $4k a month per tech. To break the ceiling near $300k a year, the advice is to build the shop so it runs without the owner, adding a part-time autoclave bench tech [Better Biomed Channel — YXLWY7VHfxM @ 00:16:13]. My target: twenty members before hiring that bench tech.

fields.name: contractor_insurance
fields.prompt: List the insurance and credential checks every subcontracted or 1099 technician must clear before going on site, and describe how you will document each check so a water-damage or liability claim never lands on your company alone.
fields.example: Before any 1099 contractor goes on site, confirm they carry their own insurance, because water-damage liability already makes dental-service coverage hard to place [Better Biomed Channel — YXLWY7VHfxM @ 00:18:38]. My checklist: proof of the contractor's own policy on file, a signed scope of work, and a training record tied to our servicing procedures.

fields.name: parts_supplier_vetting
fields.prompt: Write the vetting checklist you will apply to any remanufactured board, cable, or probe supplier, covering ISO 13485 scope, record retention, soldering certification, risk management, certificate verification, site visits, and references before a single part is installed.
fields.example: Summit Imaging says to vet suppliers for full-scope ISO 13485, not just brokering, plus retained records, IPC soldering certification and risk management, then verify certificates on ISO boards and visit the site [TechNation TV — 7d4lxsuW9Xs @ 00:59:23]. Knockoff parts running at 60% of OEM performance inflate total cost of ownership through downtime, so cheap parts rarely stay cheap.

fields.name: service_report_fields
fields.prompt: Define the fields every service report must capture before a work order closes, including complaint status, reportability review, device name, lot number, services performed, the technician, the date, related test records, and any routing into corrective and preventive action.
fields.example: Quality Systems Explained says to review each service report for complaint status and reportability, capturing device name, lot number, services done, performer, date and related test records [Quality Systems Explained — ohnyLE9h6ok @ 00:01:30]. Servicing personnel must be trained to the servicing procedures and understand customer requirements [Quality Systems Explained — ohnyLE9h6ok @ 00:01:10].

fields.name: contract_bidding_floor
fields.prompt: Before bidding against an incumbent service provider, record the prior contract price, any rival quote, and your true cost to deliver, then decide the floor below which you will walk away rather than absorb losses.
fields.example: Better Biomed Channel warns that a rival quoting about half the prior price may be padding the books for a sale [Better Biomed Channel — UQh0OoupetI @ 00:01:21]; they underbid to secure the contract, which increases their valuation [Better Biomed Channel — UQh0OoupetI @ 00:01:43]. Contracts priced below cost leave the eventual owner and the techs absorbing losses.

fields.name: analyzer_verification
fields.prompt: Record how you prove your safety analyzer and test leads before trusting any reading, including the resistance stud value, the leakage stud value, the tolerance you accept, and what you do when a reading drifts high.
fields.example: Better Biomed Channel verifies meters against a 1 ohm stud and a 100 microamp stud, which should land within about 0.5 microamp [Better Biomed Channel — HBf8beE8tGc @ 00:00:32]. If the 1 ohm reading runs high, rotate the clamp to break surface oxidation and it should stabilize close to 1 ohm [Better Biomed Channel — HBf8beE8tGc @ 00:00:49].

fields.name: safety_test_sequence
fields.prompt: List your fixed electrical safety test sequence in order, from mains voltage through protective earth, earth leakage, enclosure leakage, and applied-part leakage, and note the pass limit you will enforce at every step for each device type.
fields.example: Josh Herzka's R Series defibrillator passed at 129 microamps earth leakage against a 500 microamp limit [Better Biomed Channel — Z56Xw5_JbNs @ 00:06:06], with 6.5 microamps single-fault applied-part leakage against 50. AbishkarTECH reads mains first: a no-ground fault showed live-to-earth at 53 and neutral-to-earth at 32 against under five [AbishkarTECH — rqUE2pFiqUI @ 00:00:44].

fields.name: insulation_and_current_draw
fields.prompt: Set your insulation resistance and current draw acceptance rules, including the test voltage, the megohm value that fails a device, what an over-range reading means, and how you compare idle draw against the manufacturer's rating.
fields.example: On the Fluke ESA620 at 250 V or 500 V DC, below 2 megohms fails, 1.5 megohms fails, and OL over the 100 megohm range is good [AbishkarTECH — rqUE2pFiqUI @ 00:06:20]. The same analyzer read 0.2 A at idle, which may run higher under load, so cross-check the manufacturer's rating [AbishkarTECH — rqUE2pFiqUI @ 00:04:56].

fields.name: bench_stop_rules
fields.prompt: Write the stop rules for your bench, naming the conditions that halt a job until recalibration or service intervention, how you handle a no-power complaint beyond the fuse, and when automation can replace a manual test.
fields.example: Better Biomed Channel says never to close a no-power ticket on a fuse swap alone, because a band-aid fix always comes back [Better Biomed Channel — 7JgSRU2VyXE @ 00:08:14]. Isiah stops any job showing out-of-tolerance readings or persistent boot alarms [MedDeviceEngineerX  | Isiah — bLqvmql3QHs @ 00:05:42]. Jamie Spragus simulated a full safety test in under two minutes [TechNation TV — x772T1-4M-Q @ 00:37:50].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 2 is complete only when the rate card shows all four billing lines, every contractor and parts supplier check produces a filed document, the analyzer verification records actual 1 ohm and 100 microamp stud readings, the safety sequence lists a numeric limit for each step, and the stop rules forbid closing any no-power ticket on a fuse swap alone.

worksheets.title: The Compliance File: QMSR Readiness, Risk, Suppliers, Product Codes, Fees, and Labels
worksheets.purpose: Prepare the regulatory backbone a resale, relabeling, or servicing business needs now that the QMSR governs from February 2, 2026. Practitioners agree that certification buys no inspection exemption, risk is the thread investigators pull, and the three-letter product code decides class, pathway, and cost. This worksheet captures those decisions with dates, fees, and named owners.
instructions: Assume every procedure, management review record, and audit record you write can be read by an investigator, and draft each answer with that reader in mind.
Record dates, fee amounts, and product codes exactly as they appear on your own filings and quotes, and note the source beside each figure.
Name one responsible person for every field, so the risk file, supplier tiers, complaint escalation, and label audit each have a clear owner.
Secure the small business determination number before you buy any 510(k) cover sheet, and record that date in the fee budget field.
Re-open this worksheet after each monthly complaint review and after any new product code, supplier, or label change enters your operation.

fields.name: qmsr_transition_map
fields.prompt: Map your quality system against the February 2, 2026 QMSR switch, noting which procedures still reference the old QSR structure, where ISO 13485 language now governs, and which FDA add-ons for UDI, tracking, and corrections remain.
fields.example: AMORIT EDUCATION marks February 2, 2026 as the hard switch after a two-year transition from the February 2024 final rule [AMORIT EDUCATION — PhHUunSO_iQ @ 00:01:02]. Regulatory Compliance Associates says firms already following ISO 13485 face little change, while Part 820-only firms face significant change [Regulatory Compliance Associates — cNSAixRUu9Q @ 00:04:06].

fields.name: coverage_decision
fields.prompt: Decide whether your resale, relabeling, repackaging, or sterilizing activities pull you under the QMSR, and record the reasoning, remembering that coverage follows activity and that holding an ISO or MDSAP certificate earns no inspection exemption.
fields.example: AMORIT EDUCATION states an MDSAP or ISO certificate gives no pass on FDA inspections [AMORIT EDUCATION — PhHUunSO_iQ @ 00:02:50]. NextGenMedTech adds that Parts 800 to 1050 apply, not only Part 820 [NextGenMedTech — sB46aiZG8lw @ 00:25:39]. My note: if I relabel or repackage refurbished units, I treat the QMSR as covering that activity.

fields.name: records_language_sweep
fields.prompt: Sweep your procedures, management review minutes, internal audits, and supplier audits for any language you would not want an investigator to read, then list each document, the risky wording found, and the corrected replacement text.
fields.example: Medmarc says to sweep procedures for 'do not show to FDA' language and kill any fewer-CAPA objective, because management review and audit records are now open to inspection [Medmarc — L11OFtMOx3E @ 00:21:58]. Every blank or 'N/A' field in complaint records needs a written justification instead of being left unexplained [Medmarc — L11OFtMOx3E @ 00:25:44].

fields.name: risk_file_upkeep
fields.prompt: Describe how your risk management file stays current, which complaint trends feed it, how often you update it, and how risk links your other quality areas together, since investigators now pull that thread first during a visit.
fields.example: Matrix One says to confirm the risk management file is current and reflects the latest complaint trends, because it steers the visit [Matrix One — b_a74PE0Cn0 @ 00:03:23]. Software Connect calls risk management the link that ties the various QM areas together [Software Connect — DWOABbtgSgI @ 00:04:24]. My cadence: update the file after every monthly complaint review.

fields.name: supplier_risk_tiers
fields.prompt: Tier every supplier by risk, separating critical service providers such as contract sterilizers from off-the-shelf vendors, and set the oversight level, audit frequency, and evidence you keep for each tier as the responsible legal manufacturer.
fields.example: FDA says supplier oversight is tiered by risk, treating a contract sterilizer differently from an off-the-shelf supplier, because the legal manufacturer stays responsible for everything [U.S. Food and Drug Administration — QFNSAlfJaic @ 00:15:43]. My tiers: sterilizers and refurbishers get annual audits with retained records; packaging and generic supply vendors get a documented qualification review.

fields.name: standards_and_tools_budget
fields.prompt: Budget for the standards, software, and habit-building time your quality system needs, listing where you will buy the standards, which eQMS option you are weighing and its entry price, and how long you will monitor new habits.
fields.example: Henry flags that the free ANSI portal is view-only and that Estonia's standards are cheaper [Greenlight Guru — yW4-Hn0IXI8 @ 00:44:59]. Matrix Quality starts from 10,000 euros a year and goes live in 2 to 6 weeks [Matrix One — b_a74PE0Cn0 @ 00:04:06]. Kellerman monitors about 21 days after retraining staff [Kellerman Consulting — jUOtQFk5I3Q @ 00:30:08].

fields.name: product_code_register
fields.prompt: For every device you resell, relabel, or plan to import, record the three-letter product code, the resulting device class, the likely pathway, and any wording on your labels or marketing that could push a comparison toward De Novo.
fields.example: Easy Medical Device calls the three-letter product code probably the single most important piece of information a company needs [Easy Medical Device — USqn2QdZTCM @ 00:03:25]. leanRAQA warns a wrong code such as FXX for an antimicrobial mask is refused at RTA [leanRAQA — EnjRMOB1Uio @ 00:21:00] and advises avoiding words like 'novel' [leanRAQA — EnjRMOB1Uio @ 00:33:17].

fields.name: fda_fee_and_timeline_budget
fields.prompt: Build your FDA fee and timeline budget, listing the 510(k) user fee at standard and small-business rates, the establishment registration fee, the realistic elapsed review time, and the date you will secure a small business determination.
fields.example: Registrar Corp quotes the 2025 510(k) fee at $24,335 standard versus $6,084 small business [Registrar Corp — 9Unzt431qg8 @ 01:02:38], and establishment registration hits $11,423 in 2026. leanRAQA puts the 90-day 510(k) clock at about 200 days actual [leanRAQA — EnjRMOB1Uio @ 00:44:39]. FDA warns that paying before the SBD number means no refunds [U.S. Food and Drug Administration — cjw_q6QL1W4 @ 05:28:15].

fields.name: complaint_escalation
fields.prompt: Rewrite your complaint intake procedure so that any event possibly reportable under Part 803 is escalated immediately, and record who triages it, how documentation is captured, and how you prove the five-day report window was protected.
fields.example: FDA warns that a complaint procedure slower than immediate, such as a 10-day internal window, can miss Part 803's 5-day report [U.S. Food and Drug Administration — cjw_q6QL1W4 @ 07:25:57]. NSF says most FDA deviations come from CAPA and complaint handling [NSF — gfFy3QwozGE @ 00:35:17], and Invent Healthcare reminds that if it was not documented it did not occur.

fields.name: label_and_agent_audit
fields.prompt: Audit the labels, boxes, and import paperwork for every incoming shipment, confirming no FDA logo or printed FDA mark appears, that your US agent has a real street address, and that automated label checks get human sampling.
fields.example: Registrar Corp says to strip the FDA logo and printed FDA from labels and boxes before shipment to avoid stickering costs, delays and storage fees [Registrar Corp — 9Unzt431qg8 @ 01:15:55], and a US agent cannot use a PO box [Registrar Corp — 9Unzt431qg8 @ 00:52:04]. Henry wants automated label checks backed by a statistically significant human sample [Greenlight Guru — yW4-Hn0IXI8 @ 01:00:32].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 3 is complete only when the QMSR map cites the February 2, 2026 switch, the records sweep lists every corrected document, the risk file has a named owner and update cadence, every resold or relabeled device carries a confirmed three-letter product code, the small business determination date precedes any fee payment, and complaint escalation is immediate.

worksheets.title: 510(k) Readiness and Recall Response Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Assemble the evidence trail that gets a 510(k) past the refuse-to-accept screen on the first pass, and set up the recall, Part 806, and MAUDE discipline that protects a reseller or remanufacturer once product is in the field.
instructions: Work through the fields in order, because predicate choice shapes every later answer in this worksheet.
Cite the exact page, attachment, or record location for each claim so a reviewer can verify it within a minute.
Treat every blank cell or missing document as a gap with a named owner and a due date.
Start recall clocks on the date of the decision to act, never the date a customer letter goes out.
Revisit this worksheet before every filing, software release, or field action, and date each revision.

fields.name: predicate_lock
fields.prompt: Name the predicate device you intend to claim, record its three-letter product code, and paste its indications for use word for word. Explain why this predicate is defensible and what evidence you hold that it is not the wrong match.
fields.example: Predicate: a cleared powered patient lift sharing our product code. Indications copied verbatim from its 510(k) summary, no added adjectives. Reason: Qualio warns 15% of submissions fail on the wrong predicate [Qualio — 1GKnWm8UYVk @ 00:59:39], so we compared intended use, technology, and materials side by side, and dropped a newer candidate whose wording drifted toward novel features.

fields.name: rta_checklist_annotation
fields.prompt: List every Refuse to Accept checklist item and the exact page or attachment where each one lives inside your package. Flag any item you cannot locate in under a minute and assign an owner who will close that gap before filing.
fields.example: Item 12, biocompatibility: Attachment 7, pages 3 to 9. Item 18, level of concern: missing, owner is the software lead, due Friday. Packard says more than 50% of submissions die at RTA screening and the clock resets to zero [MedicalMarcom — -ceDuiClggg @ 00:13:03], while an annotated checklist once won acceptance on day 2 [MedicalMarcom — nUaPO0mfwKI @ 00:31:54].

fields.name: fee_and_small_business_status
fields.prompt: Record the user fee you expect to pay, whether you hold a current small business qualification, and the date you will reapply. Note who files the tax paperwork and how you will confirm approval before the cover sheet is paid.
fields.example: Packard quotes $10,953 standard versus $2,738 small business, with requalification required every year [MedicalMarcom — -ceDuiClggg @ 00:08:36]. Our controller submits on August 1st alongside the tax filing, a roughly 15-minute task, and Packard has seen approval in 5 days against the stated 60 [MedicalMarcom — -ceDuiClggg @ 00:39:20]. Cover sheet payment waits for the determination letter.

fields.name: estar_rta_triggers
fields.prompt: Confirm the two most common Refuse to Accept triggers are covered in your eSTAR: level of concern documentation and wireless coexistence testing. Also record where confidential material sits, since only the 510(k) summary attachment becomes public to anyone searching.
fields.example: Level of concern memo sits in Attachment 4, and wireless coexistence results sit in Attachment 11, because Packard sees many RTAs from missing level of concern files [Medical Device Academy — b1Ejw4mhVFU @ 00:15:58]. Supplier pricing and test vendor names go in attachments, never the eSTAR text box, since the summary is the only public attachment [Medical Device Academy — b1Ejw4mhVFU @ 00:27:42].

fields.name: traceability_drill
fields.prompt: Pick three random components or outputs from your design file and time how long it takes to trace each back to a user need. Record every empty cell in your traceability matrix and the remediation plan for closing it honestly.
fields.example: Drill result: battery housing traced to the user need for wipe-down cleaning in 40 seconds; motor controller took four minutes and failed. Saunders sets the bar at under 60 seconds and treats every empty matrix cell as a gap [Dave Saunders — 6w27HXwMbmU @ 00:13:16]. Because Saunders warns documentation cannot be created retroactively [Dave Saunders — 6w27HXwMbmU @ 00:36:12], we rerun verification instead.

fields.name: software_change_screen
fields.prompt: Describe the next software change you plan to ship and answer two questions: does a predetermined change control plan already cover it, and why are you retraining or modifying the code? State whether expanded inputs push you toward a special 510(k).
fields.example: Planned change: the algorithm will accept a second sensor input. No PCCP exists for this device, and we are retraining to add that input, which Innolitics flags as a special 510(k) trigger [Innolitics — UdQw2LB0EYc @ 00:25:57]. Decision: hold the release, draft the special 510(k), and note that the O.N. Diagnostics warning letter showed FDA staying conservative on software changes.

fields.name: review_calendar
fields.prompt: Build a realistic review calendar from submission to decision, marking the refuse-to-accept screen, the interactive review checkpoint, and the decision window. Note what internal resources must be standing by at each milestone so questions get answered within hours.
fields.example: Day 0 submit; day 15 RTA screen result; day 60 interactive review decision point; decision about 30 days after interactive review, for a realistic total of 120 to 130 days [MedicalMarcom — gGje01O9B44 @ 00:11:34]. Regulatory lead and test lab stay on call from day 55. Packard reminds us usually time is more valuable than money [MedicalMarcom — -ceDuiClggg @ 01:13:27].

fields.name: part_806_clock
fields.prompt: Record the date your firm decided to correct or remove product, the date the Part 806 report is due, and who signs it. Explain how you will avoid starting the clock at the customer letter instead of the decision.
fields.example: Decision logged March 3 by the quality director after three wheelchair motor complaints. Risk-to-health actions are reported within 10 working days [Gardner Law — aYQu_0ujhyU @ 00:12:43], and Phillips lands the report by Day 15 on the calendar, counted from the decision [Gardner Law — aYQu_0ujhyU @ 00:21:52]. Following Needelman, we file 80% of the facts on time rather than 100% late.

fields.name: recall_effectiveness_and_closure
fields.prompt: Set your recall effectiveness target, the number of contact attempts per customer, and the root cause evidence you will present for closure. Describe how you will match lot, serial, model, and dates against the official recall notice.
fields.example: Expect about 30% product return and make three good-faith attempts per customer [Medmarc — nJblY5CRIVY @ 00:39:10]. Root cause report attached, since FDA will not close a recall without one [Medmarc — nJblY5CRIVY @ 00:33:13]. Each returned bed is checked by lot, serial, model, and date against the current agency page, never screenshots [Treomark — GoXd4_jxKBg @ 00:00:33].

fields.name: maude_search_log
fields.prompt: Log every MAUDE search you run on a device you plan to buy or resell: product code, keywords, brand variants, and date ranges. Record how you bypassed the single-search cap and which records you treated as leads worth investigating.
fields.example: Searched infusion pump narratives in quarterly date ranges because MAUDE returns only 500 reports per search [Ofstead Insights — a-scTl1C2PA @ 00:08:44], then merged the Excel exports. Event-type filter left off, since malfunction reports can describe injuries [Ofstead Insights — a-scTl1C2PA @ 00:03:32]. Every hit is a lead, not causation [Expert Institute — xbxXTRwdVRs @ 00:22:47].

worksheets.completion_gate: Done only when the predicate, product code, and indications are locked, every RTA checklist item is annotated with its location, the small business determination is in hand before payment, the traceability drill passes under 60 seconds, and the Part 806 clock and MAUDE search log are dated and signed.

worksheets.title: Imaging Deinstall and Laser Handover File
worksheets.purpose: Capture the helium, site safety, service contract, and laser compliance facts that decide whether a used MRI, CT, or medical laser can be sold, shipped, and put to work without hidden costs or regulatory blocks.
instructions: Fill in one copy of this worksheet per imaging system or laser in the deal.
Record measured values, such as helium percentage and gauss line locations, rather than seller estimates.
Mark each item as verified or unverified, and do not quote a final price while any critical item is unverified.
Route electrical, blast-shield, and interlock questions to a biomed before anyone moves or powers the unit.
Attach license numbers, signed agreements, and survey results directly to the matching field.

fields.name: magnet_deinstall_plan
fields.prompt: Describe how the MRI magnet you are buying or selling will be deinstalled, stating plainly whether it stays cold and energized or gets quenched. Name who signs off on the plan and what happens if helium runs short.
fields.example: The 1.5T magnet ships cold and energized, never quenched, because quenching creates thermal shocks that can damage a system headed for the secondhand market [FGI — HPAddrORIJU @ 00:34:49]. Our lead engineer signs the plan. Helium supply is confirmed in writing with the contractor first, since quenched facilities sat down for a protracted period waiting on refills [FGI — HPAddrORIJU @ 00:32:11].

fields.name: helium_cost_model
fields.prompt: Enter the magnet's current helium level, its daily boil-off rate, and the replacement cost per liter you expect to pay. Calculate the refill exposure if the magnet quenched and the monthly boil-off cost you will build into price.
fields.example: Level reads 78 percent, above the 70 percent floor Block Imaging recommends [Block Imaging — _-e12TPIFxw @ 00:03:19]. At $20 to $30 a liter on roughly 2,000 liters, a quench risks $40,000 to $60,000 in helium alone [Block Imaging — _-e12TPIFxw @ 00:02:59]. This older unit boils off 5 to 10 liters daily, up to $500 per day [MRIPETCTSOURCE — Bu466hadTu0 @ 00:00:40].

fields.name: whole_system_inventory
fields.prompt: List everything that ships with the imaging system beyond the magnet or gantry: coils, software, service records, room requirements, and ongoing support. Mark which items you have physically verified and which still rest on the seller's word alone.
fields.example: Verified: head, knee, and spine coils, software license, and five years of service records. Unverified: shielding drawings for the buyer's room. MRIPETCTSOURCE stresses that a fill alone runs 1,200 to 1,500 liters, about $60,000 [MRIPETCTSOURCE — Bu466hadTu0 @ 00:00:40], so we price the whole system, not the magnet photo, and attach a three-year extended contract past warranty.

fields.name: ct_tube_and_service_terms
fields.prompt: For any CT system in your deal, record the tube's age, scan history, and whether a replacement tube is covered under the service agreement. Note whether the original manufacturer has issued an end-of-support letter limiting parts and engineering.
fields.example: Tube is original with no replacement history logged. Block Imaging calls the tube or glassware a major component that drives the price of a service agreement [Block Imaging — 3203LTd64a8 @ 00:00:30], so our quote includes tube coverage. The owner holds an OEM end-of-support letter, which makes the account a target for a customized extended agreement [Block Imaging — 3203LTd64a8 @ 00:01:33].

fields.name: mri_site_safety_survey
fields.prompt: Document the five gauss line survey for the buyer's site, including floors above and below the scanner. Record how Zone 3 entry will be screened and whether a whole-body ferrous-only detection system has been specified instead of hand wands.
fields.example: Five gauss line metered on all three floors and taped on the floor before Zone 3 was defined, because the field bulges through floors and ceilings [Imaging Notes — fRqZHq_Gruc @ 00:06:22]. Zone 3 entry gets a whole-body ferrous-only detector; Posh notes metal detectors are not approved for MRI use and hand wands vary between users [Metrasens — DdLolB1kuRY @ 00:57:27].

fields.name: quench_pipe_and_accident_history
fields.prompt: Record the quench-pipe discharge detail for this specific scanner model and confirm it was not copied from another manufacturer's job. Then log the MAUDE accident history search you ran, including the product code and date range used.
fields.example: Quench-pipe detail drawn fresh for the Philips unit; Gilk has seen GE details pasted onto Philips scanners even when the criteria did not match [FGI — HPAddrORIJU @ 00:13:58]. MAUDE search ran on product code LNH for the past five years, because searching MRI returns nothing while hundreds of MR events are reported annually [Metrasens — DdLolB1kuRY @ 00:47:20].

fields.name: laser_inventory_record
fields.prompt: Create the intake record for each laser you acquire: wavelength, class, serial, service history, and the trained medical laser safety officer responsible at the receiving site. Note any gaps that would block the facility from passing a CMS-grade inventory review.
fields.example: Unit: 755/1064 hair removal platform, class confirmed from the label, two prior handpiece services. The buyer's MLSO is named on the record, because Dennis says a rental operator is not your LSO and the laser safety program has to be internal [OR Today Magazine — 4yS9pDHEcIs @ 00:36:30]. Gap: no blast-shield service log, so a biomed reviews it before resale.

fields.name: interlock_and_electrical_check
fields.prompt: Record the interlock and key codes found on arrival, the new codes assigned, and the date key control was verified. Then document the electrical service the laser requires and confirm the destination room supplies it without cheater cords.
fields.example: Arrival code was 5678, the same one Dennis says everybody in the United States had [OR Today Magazine — 4yS9pDHEcIs @ 00:19:37]; reset and key control verified the same day. The unit needs a 50 amp plug, so the biomed confirmed the room before moving it, unlike the excimer laser that could not roll to the cath lab [TechNation TV — kBlmK6r6MgU @ 00:17:08].

fields.name: rental_technician_credentialing
fields.prompt: For every rental or leased laser technician entering the facility, record their laser operator credential under your own procedures and the date the business associate agreement was signed. Note what case data they may take for billing.
fields.example: Technician credentialed as a laser operator under our SOPs on June 2, with the signed BAA on file before any case data leaves for billing [OR Today Magazine — 4yS9pDHEcIs @ 00:37:22]. Certification check: we accept NCLC credentials, with a passing score of 70 and results in about two weeks [Laser Training — KPlnFyWRwTQ @ 00:06:16], not one-hour online certificates.

fields.name: jurisdiction_license_timeline
fields.prompt: If the laser ships to a licensed jurisdiction, record the possession license number, the approval to acquire, and the expected lead times. State the earliest realistic delivery date and what payment terms protect you until approval arrives.
fields.example: Queensland buyer has no laser on site, so a possession license with a clinic-specific RSPP comes first, about 2 to 3 months plus 1 to 2 weeks for approval to acquire [K-Laser Australia — Hsmu9JQR5UM @ 00:04:36]. Delivery is not allowed without it [K-Laser Australia — Hsmu9JQR5UM @ 00:05:14], so the deposit stays refundable until the license number arrives.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done only when the magnet is confirmed cold and energized with helium above 70 percent, the whole-system inventory is verified, the five gauss survey and LNH search are logged, laser codes are reset with key control verified, and every operator credential, BAA, and possession license is on file.

worksheets.title: Clinic Account Map and Sales Pipeline Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Turn veterinary, dental, and ambulatory surgery buyers into documented accounts by mapping sterile processing needs, proving cost savings line by line, and running an honest capital pipeline backed by clean outreach and recurring revenue.
instructions: Choose one live clinic account and one live capital deal before you begin, and keep both in view throughout.
Lead every account conversation with the sterile processing room, then branch into scopes, instruments, and consumables.
Show savings as line items against reimbursement, not as a single headline discount.
Record pipeline stages exactly as they stand today, and downgrade any deal that lacks a named champion.
Audit every outreach message against the field rules here before it leaves your outbox.

fields.name: central_sterile_opening
fields.prompt: Map the sterile processing room for one target clinic: autoclaves, instrument washers, processing sinks, prep-and-pack areas, and cassettes. Note which items the owner has overlooked and which you can supply as certified used units with documentation.
fields.example: Target ASC has one autoclave and no instrument washer or dedicated prep-and-pack area. We lead with Central Sterile, because many ASC owners do not realize one vendor can sell autoclaves, washers, sinks, prep-and-pack areas, and cassettes [Henry Schein Medical — VMonxNBLqE4 @ 00:05:23]. Offer: a certified used washer with service records, plus new cassettes matched to their trays.

fields.name: scope_intake_and_leak_test
fields.prompt: For every endoscope you take in, record the distal end and bending rubber inspection, the leak test result, and whether air was flushed from the channels first. Classify the repair as a minor bending rubber fix or full rebuild.
fields.example: Distal end clean; bending rubber shows a small tooth cut. Pressure tested before immersion [Surgical Direct (Surgical Direct) — DrTCjk0roNk @ 00:01:04], channels flushed of air, no enzymatic cleaner added beforehand [Surgical Direct (Surgical Direct) — DrTCjk0roNk @ 00:08:18]. Steady champagne bubbles at the cut confirmed a real leak, caught early enough for a bending rubber repair instead of a rebuild.

fields.name: pack_release_standard
fields.prompt: Write the release standard your veterinary or surgical buyer uses before a sterile pack leaves processing: indicator tape, inner indicator strip, gauze count, wrap layers, and shelf life. Note which consumables this standard burns through each week.
fields.example: Release only when outer tape shows black stripes and the inner strip has changed [Four Paws Animal Hospital & Wellness Center — PlDJXzo7cN4 @ 00:03:52], with an exact gauze count inside. Triple-wrapped packs unused after six months get rewashed, repacked, and resterilized [PEER at TAMU — WoO-cNElJpg @ 00:20:10]. Weekly burn: indicator tape, strips, wraps, and ultrasonic solution.

fields.name: surgeon_line_item_comparison
fields.prompt: Build a line-item cost comparison for one surgeon or procedure at your target ambulatory surgery center. List the current price of each tray item, your alternative price, and the savings per case against the facility's reimbursement.
fields.example: Total knee: trays standardized from five to two [American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons — AQIyPCz9bJM @ 00:23:06]. Blade line: $85 current versus $45 alternative, the exact question surgeons asked once costs were shown per surgeon [American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons — AQIyPCz9bJM @ 00:26:08]. Target: $750 saved per case against a roughly $8,400 Medicare knee.

fields.name: dental_account_web
fields.prompt: Sketch the referral web around one dental client: the oral surgeons, orthodontists, and periodontists they refer to. Note the compliance exposures each practice carries, including patient record request deadlines, and which relationship you will approach next.
fields.example: Anchor client refers to two oral surgeons and one orthodontist; dentists refer tightly, so one relationship compounds into several accounts [Nuronus — iAwNQ3QON9c @ 00:02:30]. Each office gets a records-request checklist, since Gums Dental Care was fined seventy thousand dollars with no breach [Nuronus — iAwNQ3QON9c @ 00:00:24]. Next approach: the orthodontist, who just bought a new autoclave.

fields.name: instrument_quality_tier
fields.prompt: Decide which instrument and sterilization accessory tiers you will stock for clinic buyers, from premium instruments built to last decades to low-cost cassettes and soak boxes. Record the price points, expected lifespan, and care rules you will hand buyers.
fields.example: Budget tier: soak boxes from $5.23 and trays up to about $21 [LopinMoetas — 8kG0BUAGcP4 @ 00:00:33]. Premium tier: German surgical instruments sold for decades of use. Every kit ships with a care card warning that instruments should never sit overnight in the ultrasonic cleaner or milk, since they can rust [Vet Candy | Veterinary Education, CE & News — Zb4YYmRy5x0 @ 00:10:28].

fields.name: capital_pipeline_funnel
fields.prompt: List the capital equipment accounts in your pipeline, the stage each has truthfully reached, and the champion inside each one. Calculate how many accounts you need to reach your purchase order goal, and note any stage you are tempted to inflate.
fields.example: Goal: four imaging purchase orders. Licata's funnel says 30 accounts yield 1 to 2 purchase orders [Joe Licata | Medical Sales Coach — KsMhJhbA73k @ 00:37:42], so we need roughly 60 to 120 accounts. Two late-stage deals lack a champion and get downgraded, because managers carry pipeline straight to the board [Joe Licata | Medical Sales Coach — KsMhJhbA73k @ 00:34:00].

fields.name: vac_presentation_plan
fields.prompt: Plan how your physician champion will present your equipment to the value analysis committee. Record the in-service date relative to the meeting, the ROI model you will hand the CFO, and the struggles you uncovered indirectly.
fields.example: VAC meets Thursday; in-service set for Tuesday, because reps are barred and the physician presents: if you don't remember, they won't [Joe Licata | Medical Sales Coach — KsMhJhbA73k @ 00:14:21]. Struggles surfaced by asking whether the surgeon faced the same problem Dr B described [New to Medical Device Sales — PaW-3LfksaU @ 00:07:29]. CFO model shows service and consumables revenue.

fields.name: outreach_message_audit
fields.prompt: Paste the next outreach message you plan to send to a hiring manager, clinic owner, or buyer. Audit its word count, strip leftover AI dashes, confirm connection requests carry no note, and check your profile badges before sending anything.
fields.example: Message trimmed to 82 words, under the 100-word ceiling. Dashes removed, since AI dashes are the top complaint Jacob hears from hiring managers [New to Medical Device Sales — G5Dl1131xAw @ 00:35:06]. Connection request sent with no note [New to Medical Device Sales — G5Dl1131xAw @ 00:30:02], and the open to work badge came off [Med Sales With Matt — 2Nn9rL0ZXRg @ 00:03:11].

fields.name: recurring_revenue_after_sale
fields.prompt: For each machine you sell or place, list the service contract, consumables, and utilization revenue that follow the sale. Note any pricing ceiling payers will tolerate, and confirm you have not priced at the full incremental cost you solve.
fields.example: Placed unit: refurbished patient monitor package. Recurring lines: annual service contract, monthly consumables, and per-use supplies. The problem it solves costs the clinic about $20K incrementally, but pricing stays well below that to leave payer headroom [Fast Forward Medical Innovation – Commercialization Education — oAV1SBup8Q8 @ 00:34:59]. Contract terms avoid surprises, because discounts vanish, penalties do not [Hidden Industries — uNFHZlCznIw @ 00:02:48].

worksheets.completion_gate: Done only when one clinic's sterile processing room is mapped, scope intake and pack release standards are written, a line-item savings sheet exists for one surgeon, the pipeline math covers your purchase order goal with honest stages, and every outbound message passes the audit.
